text:
leah: Hey @tom @raj — AcmeHealth sent back the DPA with three asks that block sign-off: a simple dataflow showing where embeddings & user content live, confirmation on whether raw PII can be reconstructed from embeddings, and KMS key provenance for BYOK. They want answers by EOD.

onboard-bot: Ticket CH-8247 created and assigned to customer-success (leah). SLA: 48h.

tom: quick clarity — they're on hosted (redwood cloud) today, correct? that affects BYOK availability.

leah: yes hosted today, potentially Dedicated next quarter.

mike: engineering short answer (for customer): we do not persist raw PII as a distinct, reversible artifact. Embeddings are numeric vectors stored in our encrypted blob store (default TTL 90 days, configurable per account). Current research indicates embeddings are not practically reversible to original text.

raj: security addendum: BYOK is offered only for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, keys are managed by Redwood KMS; we can export KMS provenance and audit logs tied to the service account. Recommend customers pseudonymize or redact direct identifiers before sending if they need stronger guarantees.

tom: drafting a concise reply for Leah — will paste below. please review.

mike: add retention & deletion SLO: we log deletion events and they propagate to audit logs within 24h.

raj: also say we never index whole request bodies in long-term logs — only minimal metadata for billing/metrics. we can sign a limited DPA addendum for embeddings retention if they require it.

mike: ops confirm they can produce a KMS provenance snapshot within 48h if requested.

leah: Draft reply to customer (one para):
"Hi — thanks for the questions. Short answers: embeddings are stored as numeric vectors in our encrypted store (default TTL 90 days, can be configured). We do not store raw PII as a reversible artifact; current analyses show embeddings are not practically reversible to original text. For hosted deployments encryption keys are managed by Redwood KMS; BYOK is available on Dedicated/Private only. We can provide KMS provenance logs and a retention addendum on request. We recommend masking direct identifiers before sending if you require minimization. Attached is a simple dataflow snapshot and a link to our SOC2 data-handling doc. Happy to set up a quick call if helpful. — Leah, Customer Success"

leah: Attached ascii dataflow for their diagram:
```
user -> redwood-api -> tokenizer -> model -> embedding-store (encrypted, TTL=90d)
                     -> ephemeral logs (48h)
backup -> encrypted-blob-storage (access via KMS)
```

tom: wording tweak done, SGTM. raj/mike any other blockers?

raj: no blockers. send and mark onboarding status: evidence requested on renewal tracker.

leah: sending now. thanks everyone :heart:
